thread:
jonathan: Heads-up — nightly perf job (runtime-e2e/gpu) shows steady GPU memory growth after the kernel-selector change landed.
jonathan: Saw this first on the smoke harness: run #42 -> worker 3 goes from 6.9GB -> 11.2GB over 20 minutes and never frees between requests.
jonathan: repro steps i used:
```
# checkout the change
git checkout feat/kernel-selector-heuristics
# run tiny repro harness (inside docker:runtime-test)
python tests/repro/mem_growth_smoketest.py --model small --iters 500 --batch 1
``` 
jonathan: attached a short heap snapshot (PTRS and slab summary) and a timeline from nvprof: https://internal/artifacts/1932107890/heap-snap-1
maria: interesting — is the growth linear with requests or jumps after certain kernels? can you paste the nvprof snippet?
jonathan: nvprof excerpt (trimmed):
```
Time(sec)  TotalAlloc(MB)
0.0        7000
60.0       7300
120.0      7600
300.0      11200
``` 
jonathan: pattern looks like stable then sudden jump when the runtime switches kernel variant for attention (long_seq path)
maria: ok that smells like workspace resize or a new kernel path allocating a large temporary and not releasing it — could be allocator fragmentation or an unpaired alloc/free in the fallback path.
devon: fwiw i reproduced quickly. increasing env var WORKSPACE_GROWTH_LIMIT=1.0 makes the jumps larger. setting WORKSPACE_GROWTH_LIMIT=0.5 reduces the jump magnitude.
devon: quick hypothesis: kernel-selector now routes some sequences to the optimized long-seq kernel that uses a persistent scratch buffer per-stream. if we forget to register that buffer with the slab allocator free path on fallback we leak.
jonathan: good call. i grepped for register_buffer/free_buffer calls in the new selector code — i see register on hot path but not in the fallback branch (line 312). failing to register would keep ownership with a stack pointer that isn't tracked.
maria: can you paste the minimal repro patch to show the missing call? a 5-line diff would help
devon: patch I tested locally (fake example):
```
- if (use_optimized) alloc_scratch(...);
+ if (use_optimized) alloc_scratch(...);
+ else if (fallback_alloc) register_scratch_with_slab(...);
```
devon: also ran `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMPOOL=1` to rule out the cuda mempool behaviour — leak still present but smaller. suggests our allocator/slab bookkeeping is the culprit, not just cuda caching.
jonathan: started a bisect to find first bad commit: `git bisect start -- bad good` -> currently at 6e3a7.. might take a bit.
maria: parallel asks: can we get an allocator profile (slab histograms) for the failing run? `./bin/allocator-telemetry --dump-histogram > hist.json` would be perfect.
jonathan: uploaded hist.json to the artifact link above. key bits: many ~16MB slabs gone to 'in-use' and not freed, and a spike in 'temporary_workspace' owner tag.
infra-bot: @channel nightly job runtime-e2e/gpu-smoke started (id: job-1932107900). Will annotate results here when done.
jonathan: i also noticed kvcache eviction count is zero during the run; maybe code path bypasses kvcache free on fallback. devon, can you add a quick assert in the kvcache path to log `evict_count` inside fallback?
devon: added log, pushed to `debug/kernel-fallback-log`. link: https://internal/ci/changes/3240
maria: small experiment suggestion: try forcing kernel selection to always choose the long_seq kernel without fallback (so no allocation on fallback) — if that stabilizes mem, it's definitely the fallback branch.
jonathan: ran that experiment — forcing long_seq makes mem stable (no jumps). forcing short_seq also stable. only mixed routing causes leak.
devon: ok that pins it to interaction between route-changes and allocator registration. probable cause: we allocate a scratch buffer then immediately replace it on fallback but never call slab_free for the replaced pointer. allocator tracks the pointer as live.
maria: quick mitigation: add a defensive slab_free in all fallback branches (even if pointer null-check). then run the smoke tests overnight.
jonathan: applied patch `fix/fallback-ensure-free` and ran local 2-hour smoketest — no growth observed (0.2% noise).
infra-bot: CI job job-1932107900 finished: runtime-e2e/gpu-smoke — FAILED in step `perf-smoke` (OOM on worker3) — logs: https://internal/ci/job-1932107900/log
srebot: alert: OOM spikes observed in job-1932107900 for service runtime-smoke; incident ticket created INC-2026-1931
maria: hmm CI OOM despite local pass — could be race or different workload. devon, can you instrument slab allocator to emit owner tags on each free and log any double-alloc without free? small cost but helpful.
devon: added verbose allocator traces; triggered a CI run on debug branch `fix/fallback-ensure-free+debug`. ticket linked: https://internal/ci/changes/3250
jonathan: tracing output shows a case where fallback path replaces pointer A with B but B was registered under a different stream id; free for A is never invoked because we overwritten metadata before free call.
maria: that's a metadata overwrite bug — we should snapshot the old pointer before overwriting and call slab_free on it. devon, can you prepare a tiny atomic swap+free guard?
devon: pushing small change: read-modify-free sequence with CAS to be safe in concurrent envs. also added `ASSERT(!double_free)` in debug mode. pushing now.
infra-bot: scheduled debug run job-1932111200 for branch `fix/fallback-ensure-free+debug`.
jonathan: after merging CAS-fix we ran full smoke for 6 hours on a repro fleet: memory stable across all workers. no OOMs.
maria: excellent — next steps: 1) cut a small patch release to staging with the fix, 2) run overnight perf suite, 3) prepare postmortem blurb for eng-runtime channel with root cause and mitigation.
devon: added unit test that simulates rapid kernel flip and asserts slab refcounts stable.
jonathan: putting PR up: https://internal/git/pulls/4520 — reviewers: @maria @devon. marking as high-risk-change but small fix.
maria: when we cut staging, let's also add an automated smoke that storms kernel selection switches to catch regressions early.
jonathan: noted. thanks team :thumbsup:
